title: Five-minute work bursts
steps: Pick one small task (one worksheet row). Set a visible 5-minute timer. Work until it rings, then give a 2-minute movement break. Repeat up to 3 times.
avoid: Do not add extra tasks if finished early.

title: One instruction at a time
steps: Get the child's eyes, say ONE short instruction, ask them to say it back, then let them do it. Add a second step only after three clean successes.
avoid: Avoid giving instructions from another room.

title: Chunked homework plan
steps: Split homework into 3 chunks with a tick-list. Start with the shortest. After each chunk: 3-minute break away from screens. Child ticks the list themselves.
avoid: Do not keep the phone or TV in the room.

title: Bag-and-routine checklist
steps: Make a 5-picture or 5-word checklist (bottle, tiffin, books, copy, pencil box) for the door. Child checks it each evening. Praise the check, not the result.
avoid: Do not pack the bag for the child every day.

title: Quiet work corner
steps: Set one fixed, tidy spot for homework: facing a wall, away from TV and traffic, with only what is needed on the table.

title: Home and class notes for the professional
steps: For one week jot down when the difficulty happens (time, subject, place) and what helped. Take it to the school counsellor, special educator or doctor.

title: Say it back
steps: Give a 2-step instruction ('pick up the book and put it on the table'). Ask the child to say it back, then do it. Grow to 3 steps slowly.
avoid: Do not test; keep it playful.

title: Picture story retell
steps: Look at 3 simple pictures in order. Ask 'what happened first, next, last?' Model a full sentence, ask the child to try. Praise attempts.

title: Explain the day
steps: At dinner each person tells one thing from the day with 'who, what, where, why'. Help with a prompt only after a pause.

title: Word-finding games
steps: Play 'name 5 things that are round / sold in a market / found in a kitchen'. Give a first-sound hint if stuck.

title: Face-to-face talking
steps: Get down to the child's eye level, speak slowly in short sentences, pause, and wait a full 5 seconds before repeating.

title: Hearing and speech check route
steps: Ask the school health team (RBSK), a paediatrician or DEIC for a hearing check and a speech-language assessment.

title: Sound of the day
steps: Pick one letter sound. Find 5 objects that start with it, say them slowly, then blend 'c-a-t'. Use the home language and the school language.
avoid: Do not force reading aloud in front of others.

title: Rhyme and clap
steps: Clap syllables of names and words. Make rhymes (cat, mat, hat). Rhyme games build the sound awareness reading depends on.

title: Paired reading
steps: Read a page together aloud at the same pace, then let the child continue alone; when they stumble, read along again. Pick short, interesting text.
avoid: Do not interrupt for every error.

title: Ruler under the line
steps: Use a ruler or finger under the line while reading to help keep the place. Re-read the same short passage 3 times to build fluency.

title: Ten minutes daily
steps: Read for 10 minutes every day, a mix of the child's choice and a little challenge. Keep it calm and positive.

title: Learning assessment route
steps: Ask the school special educator or counsellor, or the DEIC / a paediatrician, about a learning (reading) assessment.

title: Big-to-small letter shapes
steps: Practise letters first in the air, then in sand or on a tray, then on paper with guide lines. Start every letter from the top.
avoid: Do not require neatness for long stretches.

title: Dough and clip play
steps: Roll dough, use tongs or clothes-pegs to move small items. Builds the hand strength needed for writing.

title: Short daily sentence
steps: Write 2-3 sentences about the day. Check one thing only (e.g., full stop). Praise the ideas first.

title: Spelling in chunks
steps: Practise 3 words a day: look, say in syllables, cover, write, check. Revise the same words on day 3 and day 7.

title: Comfortable setup
steps: Check seat height, paper tilt and pencil grip (a soft grip helps). Allow short breaks every few lines.

title: Handwriting / learning assessment route
steps: Ask the school special educator, an occupational therapist or a paediatrician whether a writing or learning assessment is needed.

title: Count and compare with objects
steps: Count real objects (beans, coins, buttons). Ask 'which group has more?' Make and break groups of up to 10.
avoid: Do not rely on rote tables first.

title: Number line walk
steps: Draw a 0-20 number line on the floor. Hop to add, hop back to subtract.

title: Money and time in real life
steps: Let the child pay for a small item and check change; read the clock for meals and bus times.

title: Tables with patterns
steps: Learn tables through patterns (2s, 5s, 10s first; 9s finger trick) and short daily practice, not long drills.

title: Fear-free maths
steps: Praise effort and method, not speed. Let the child explain how they got an answer, right or wrong.

title: Learning assessment route
steps: Ask the school special educator or a paediatrician about an assessment of maths learning.

title: Ball and balance play
steps: Roll, throw and catch a large soft ball; walk along a line; stand on one foot for a count of 5. Make it a game.

title: Scissors and threading
steps: Cut along thick lines, then curves; thread large beads. Slowly make lines thinner.

title: Cycle, skip, swim
steps: Pick one whole-body skill the child likes (cycling, skipping rope, swimming) and practise a little most days.

title: Everyday tasks
steps: Practise buttons, zips, laces and tying a knot with a slow demo, then hand-over-hand, then alone.

title: Success-first practice
steps: Start with tasks the child can do and make them slightly harder. Let the child choose the activity.

title: Therapy assessment route
steps: Ask a paediatrician, the RBSK school team or DEIC about an occupational therapy / physiotherapy assessment.

title: Turn-taking games
steps: Play simple board or card games with one sibling or friend. Use words: 'my turn', 'your turn', 'good try'.

title: Feelings faces
steps: Look at pictures or faces and name the feeling. Ask 'what might they want?'

title: One friend, one plan
steps: Arrange a small, structured play date (one child, one activity). Rehearse greetings and how to join a game.
avoid: Avoid big crowded parties at first.

title: Role-play a tricky moment
steps: Act out being left out or disagreeing. Practise 2 calm things to say and 1 adult to tell.

title: Shared-interest group
steps: Join a small club (art, football, chess) where friendships grow around something the child likes.

title: Talk to the school counsellor
steps: Share what you see with the class teacher and counsellor, including any teasing or bullying, so they can watch and support.

title: Name it, then calm it
steps: When upset, name the feeling ('you look angry'). Then use a short calm routine: 5 slow 'smell the flower, blow the candle' breaths.
avoid: Do not argue during the meltdown; talk after.

title: Morning goodbye routine
steps: Use the same short goodbye every day (hug, phrase, wave). Stay calm, leave on time, and keep the promise about pick-up.

title: Worry time
steps: Set 10 minutes a day to write or draw worries, pick one, and plan one small step. Outside that time, park worries on paper.

title: Predictable routine
steps: Keep sleep, meal and homework times steady; limit screens at night; build in one daily play or exercise slot.

title: Notice and praise coping
steps: Notice and praise the moments the child handles a hard feeling well. Keep a short note of triggers and times.

title: Talk to a counsellor
steps: Speak with the school counsellor, a paediatrician or a child mental-health service. Kiran (1800-599-0019, free) can help you find support.
